After select_edges_by_node on B, the three edges touching B (A–B, B–C, and B–E) are selected in the accent color; B itself is outlined as the named node but is not selected." width="100%"} Selects every edge with at least one endpoint in the given node list. In directed graphs both incoming and outgoing edges are included; direction is not considered. Edges *between* two listed nodes are selected once, like any other incident edge. This is a quick way to grab the local connectivity around specific nodes, for example to: - inspect all relationships of a node with `get_edge_df_ws()` - delete every edge touching a node (isolating it but keeping the node) with `delete_edges_ws()` - restyle or tag the edges around a node of interest with `set_edge_attrs_ws()` Only edges are selected; the listed nodes themselves are not, and any node selection is cleared. To select only edges in one direction, use `select_edges()` with a predicate on `e.source` or `e.target`. The edges are added to the current selection, unless `set_op=` says otherwise. The graph is modified in place and returned for chaining. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [nodes]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[int | str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A list of nodes whose incident edges should be selected. Each item can be an integer node ID or a string label, and the two forms can be mixed. All of them are resolved first, so an unknown ID or label raises `ValueError` without changing the selection. An empty list selects nothing. [set_op]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["union"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : How these edges combine with the current edge selection. `"union"` (default) adds them to it, `"replace"` makes them the selection, `"intersect"` keeps only the selected edges among them, and `"difference"` removes them from it. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The same graph (modified in place) for method chaining. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If an ID or label in `nodes=` is not found in the graph, or if `set_op=` is not `"union"`, `"replace"`, `"intersect"`, or `"difference"`. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Selecting "B" pulls in every edge that touches it -- both `A-B` and `B-C`, but not the unrelated `C-D` edge: ::: {#f4f8db24 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D"]) .add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "D")]) ) b_id = graph.get_id_from_label("B") graph.select_edges_by_node([b_id]) graph.count_selected_edges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 2 ``` ::: ::: Labels work just as well as IDs, and several nodes can be given at once. Selecting around "A" and "D" picks up `A-B` and `C-D`, leaving the middle edge `B-C` alone: ::: {#8843d67e .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph.clear_selection() graph.select_edges_by_node(["A", "D"]) graph.get_edge_df_ws() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}
